interface.name: zopenlook_decoration_manager_v1

description.summary: create OpenLook-style chrome for another client's window

interface.description:
Standard Wayland deliberately gives a client no way to learn another client's window position, or to attach a surface to another client's surface. That makes it impossible for an ordinary client to draw decoration chrome around windows it doesn't own -- exactly what olshell needs to do for OpenLook-style title bars, since olcore (the design's privileged half) is meant to stay ignorant of OpenLook's visual style.
This protocol bridges that gap. olshell identifies which toplevel to decorate using the handle it already holds from wlr-foreign-toplevel-management-unstable-v1, and supplies its own plain wl_surface (created via wl_compositor, exactly as for any other olshell-owned surface). The compositor -- which does have access to both surfaces -- takes over positioning and stacking that surface relative to the toplevel, the same way wlr-layer-shell takes over positioning a plain surface relative to an output.
Warning! The protocol described in this file is currently in the testing phase. Backward compatible changes may be added together with the corresponding interface version bump. Backward incompatible changes can only be done by bumping the major version number in the protocol and interface names.

request.name: get_decoration

description.summary: create a header decoration for a toplevel

request.description:
Assigns surface to be the header (title bar) decoration for toplevel. surface must be a freshly-created wl_surface with no buffer and no other role. height is olshell's fixed preferred header height in surface-local pixels; olcore does not second-guess it.
Only one header decoration may exist per toplevel at a time, and toplevel must currently be mapped. Violating either sends the already_decorated or no_such_toplevel protocol error and leaves the new object inert (any request on it is ignored).

request.name: grab_keyboard

description.summary: request seat keyboard focus for one of olshell's own surfaces

request.description:
Grants keyboard focus to surface -- any wl_surface belonging to this client, typically a window-menu popup or one of its submenus (subsurfaces of a header obtained via get_decoration). wlr-layer-shell's Exclusive keyboard interactivity gives the root menu this same ability directly; a decoration's header and the popups hanging off it are plain subsurfaces with no equivalent of their own, hence this request. Replaces whatever surface previously had focus, olshell-owned or not.
Focus is given back to the most-recently-focused toplevel (see focus_toplevel) as soon as either surface is destroyed or release_keyboard is called, whichever happens first -- callers that always destroy surface promptly when they're done with it (as olshell does today) never need to call release_keyboard explicitly.

request.name: release_keyboard

description.summary: give back keyboard focus taken by grab_keyboard

request.description: A no-op if the surface from the most recent grab_keyboard call no longer has focus for some other reason (e.g. it was already destroyed, or a later grab_keyboard call replaced it).

request.name: destroy
request.description: Destroys this manager object. Does not affect any decorations already created through it, or a keyboard grab in progress.

entry.name: no_such_toplevel
entry.summary: the handle does not name a currently-mapped toplevel

entry.name: already_decorated
entry.summary: the toplevel already has a header decoration

interface.name: zopenlook_decoration_v1

description.summary: a header decoration attached to one toplevel

interface.description: Follows the same configure/ack_configure pattern as xdg_surface and zwlr_layer_surface_v1: after creation, and again whenever the decorated toplevel's width changes, the compositor sends a configure event; olshell resizes its buffer to match, then attaches/commits it and acks the configure by serial.

request.name: move

description.summary: begin an interactive move of the decorated toplevel

request.description:
Tells olcore to start moving the decorated toplevel, following the pointer -- the same interactive move a client can normally only trigger on its own xdg_toplevel, exposed here so olshell can trigger it too (on behalf of a toplevel it doesn't own) from two different gestures: dragging the header directly, and the window menu's Move item.
Those two gestures end differently, which held says which: a header drag is still holding its triggering button down when this is sent, so the move should end when that button is released, like a normal drag (held = 1). The window menu's Move item is a discrete click -- by the time olshell has processed the click and sent this request, that button is already gone, so there's nothing to release; the move instead ends on the *next* fresh press anywhere, click-to-arm/click-to-confirm style (held = 0).
olcore can't reliably infer this itself: whether the triggering button still reads as held by the time this request is processed depends on IPC scheduling, not on which gesture actually happened (confirmed live -- it read "held" for both).

arg.name: held
arg.summary: 1 if the triggering button is still held, 0 otherwise

request.name: resize

description.summary: begin an interactive resize of the decorated toplevel

request.description: Tells olcore to start resizing the decorated toplevel from the given edge or corner -- the same interactive resize a client can normally only trigger on its own xdg_toplevel, exposed here for the same reason move is. edges is a bitmask of the edge enum below; olshell has no resize-corner chrome yet, so its only caller (the window menu's Resize item) always passes bottom|right. held has the same meaning and rationale as move's held argument.

arg.name: held
arg.summary: 1 if the triggering button is still held, 0 otherwise

request.name: lower

description.summary: lower the decorated toplevel to the bottom of the stack

request.description: Instant, not a grab -- unlike move/resize there's no pointer tracking involved. The window menu's Back item is the only caller.

request.name: quit

description.summary: close every toplevel belonging to the same client as this one

request.description: Like xdg_toplevel's own close, sent to the decorated toplevel and every other mapped toplevel that shares its client connection -- i.e. the same running application instance, not just a matching app_id (two separately-launched instances of the same app must stay independent). Still a polite request, same as a single close; the client(s) decide how to respond. The window menu's Quit item is the only caller.

request.name: toggle_sticky

description.summary: toggle whether the toplevel is visible on every workspace

request.description: A sticky toplevel stays visible regardless of which workspace is active, exempt from the hiding switching workspaces normally causes. Un-sticking commits the toplevel to whichever workspace is active at that moment, rather than reverting to wherever it was before it was stuck (which could easily no longer be the active one, making the toplevel appear to vanish). Toggles current state rather than taking an explicit target; olcore reports the result via sticky_changed, so olshell doesn't need to track which direction to ask for -- it can always just ask for the opposite of whatever it was last told. The window menu's Stick item is the only caller.

request.name: destroy
request.description: The header disappears immediately. The underlying wl_surface is unaffected and may be destroyed separately by olshell.

event.name: configure

description.summary: suggest a size for the header

event.description:
width tracks the decorated toplevel's current width and is authoritative -- olshell should size its buffer to exactly width x height. height simply echoes back what get_decoration was called with.
toplevel_height is the decorated toplevel's own current content height -- not the header's, which is always just height. olshell has no other way to learn this (wlr-foreign-toplevel-management deliberately carries no geometry), and needs it to position chrome relative to the toplevel's bottom edge, e.g. bottom resize-corner handles, as subsurfaces of the header positioned far enough down to reach it.

event.name: closed
event.description: Sent once, when the toplevel this decoration is attached to is unmapped or destroyed. olshell should destroy this object (and may destroy or recycle the underlying wl_surface) in response; olcore has already dropped its own reference to it.

event.name: sticky_changed

description.summary: report the result of a toggle_sticky request

event.description: Sent once, right after processing a toggle_sticky request, with the toplevel's new sticky state -- there's no separate query request, since the only way this ever changes is toggle_sticky itself, so olshell already knows a response is coming.
